title: Cost Simulator Sandbox — Prompt Economizer (scratchpad)
content:
Goal:
Quick, interactive simulator that lets engineers and product folks estimate token/cost/latency trade-offs for prompt edits, batching, caching and routing choices without hitting production endpoints. Focus on a lightweight dev-research sandbox that can be embedded in Console or run locally as a tiny web app.

Why this exists (notes to self):
- Teams waste time running expensive experiments against prod to get cost estimates.
- Nonlinear factors (batching, KV prefix reuse, quantization) make naive per-token estimates inaccurate.
- Want something to expose realistic deltas so PM/POs can justify batching/caching investments.

Primary personas:
- Product engineer: wants a quick answer for proposed prompt change (how much more/less will it cost at scale).
- Platform engineer: validate impact of autoscale/burst policies on unit cost.
- Solutions engineer / customer: show customers potential savings from switching to Dedicated/Private.

High-level features (MVP):
1) Prompt input area + sample chat history option (to estimate prefix re-use).
2) Knobs: model family (gpt-like / open-llama / redwood-verified-small), quantization (none / 8-bit / 4-bit), batch size distribution, cache hit rate %, prefix reuse length, avg reply tokens, streaming on/off.
3) Backend sim engine: simple cost/latency model with configurable coefficients derived from measured profiles.
4) Result summary: per-request token-count breakdown, estimated $/1M requests, latency percentile estimates, and sensitivity sliders showing which knob moves cost most.
5) Compare runs: side-by-side diffs (current vs proposed prompt or model).
6) Export: JSON report + reproducible API snippet (curl/SDK) for running an equivalent workload.

Rough UX flow
- Paste prompt or upload sample convo (or choose canned examples).
- Set traffic pattern (requests/minute, concurrency) and percent of requests that are cached/have prefix reuse.
- Toggle model/quantization/batching.
- Click "Simulate" -> show summary + expanded breakdown.

User stories
- As a product engineer, I want to paste a prompt and see estimated cost-per-1000-requests for the hosted API so I can decide whether to shorten system prompt.
- As a platform engineer, I want to model the effect of increasing batch size from 1 to 8 on 95th percentile latency and cost per token so I can tune autoscale policies.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to generate an exportable report that I can attach to a customer proposal showing potential savings from Dedicated.

Simulation model (initial heuristics)
- Base per-token compute cost (model dependent): c_base(model) in $ per token. (populate with representative numbers in calibration step)
- Quantization multiplier: q_mul = {none:1, 8-bit:0.5, 4-bit:0.35}
- Effective tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens * streaming_factor (streaming reduces some tail compute cost?) — treat streaming as small latency change, keep cost per output token roughly same but show latency reduction.
- Batching factor: batch_efficiency = 1 - (alpha / batch_size) where alpha ~ 0.3 (tunable).
- Cache hit: tokens_saved = prefix_reuse_tokens * cache_hit_rate.
- Routing fallback cost: if primary region out, fallback to cheaper/higher-latency model with ratio r.

Example calculation (toy numbers)
- model: redwood-small: c_base=0.0000015 $/token
- prompt tokens: 120 (system+history), response tokens: 80 avg
- quantization 8-bit -> q_mul=0.5 -> per-token = 0.00000075
- cache hit 40% with prefix 80 tokens -> tokens_saved per request = 32
- effective tokens = (120+80)-32 = 168
- cost per request = 168 * 0.00000075 = $0.000126 -> $126 per 1M requests
- batch_size=4 -> batch_efficiency=1 - 0.3/4 = 0.925 -> adjusted cost per request ~= 0.0001166 (approx).

Metrics we should surface
- $ per X requests (1k/100k/1M)
- Avg / P95 / P99 latency estimate (ms) given concurrency and batch distribution
- Token breakdown graph (system / user / response / cached saved)
- Sensitivity waterfall (how much each knob moves cost)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Sim runs within 2s for typical inputs (small web UI).
- Simulation math documented in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts).
- Export JSON includes all knobs + computed summary + timestamp.
- At least 3 canned examples (chatbot, summarization, search-re-rank) included.

Edge cases / constraints / caveats to surface to users
- This is an estimator — measured production costs will vary; include margin of error +/- 10-30% depending on model and batch.
- Quantization savings vary with model architecture; make it configurable per-model.
- Prefix reuse effectiveness depends on real user behavior. Provide guidance: a) instrument telemetry to measure real reuse rate; b) feed measured reuse into simulator.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Start with a client-side sim that runs deterministic math (no infra). Reason: fastest iteration and no infra cost.
- Add server-side profile calibration job that pulls measured telemetry (avg tokens, cache_hit %) for teams who opt-in; will refine baseline coefficients.
- Store canned example set as static JSON in repo.
- Expose SDK snippet generator that uses Redwood API keys and includes recommended headers/timeout.

Open questions / decisions
- Should simulator model tail latency increases from larger context lengths explicitly (token growth -> memory thrash)? Probably later.
- How to present uncertainty in a simple way — single +/- slider or multiple buckets? Start with one configurable margin.
- Do we show monetary estimates for both Hosted and Dedicated side-by-side? Users find that helpful but we need a good Dedicated cost model (committed vs burst billing).

Next steps (short):
- prototyping spike: build single-page React sim with knobs and 3 canned examples (owner: me). 1 week.
- calibrate model coefficients from perf dashboards (ask SRE/observability for token/latency profiles). (Lena)
- design small export template for Solutions reports (Mika)

Notes to self (brain-dump):
- nice-to-have: playback mode where you can feed a small sample of real traffic (CSV of prompts) and get aggregated sim results. Would be killer for sales demos.
- think about a "what-if" slider that shows cost delta if you reduce system prompt by X tokens (so PMs can see marginal impact of removing a single sentence).
- maybe surface suggested optimizations automatically (e.g., compress system prompt, enable kv cache for repeated instructions, switch to 8-bit quant).

References / links to check later:
- CONFLUENCE-1267 (cost modeling guidelines)
- JIRA-INF-9821 (telemetry export for tokens by route)
- Slack thread: #runtime-costs msg-abc123 (conversation about batch efficiency numbers)

TODO (personal):
- [ ] mock up UI in figma (quick)
- [ ] implement client-side sim prototype
- [ ] chat with SRE for baseline numbers
- [ ] add 3 canned examples + description text
- [ ] write short demo script for Solutions team

End of scratchpad.
